stories.summary: The publication-input grammar correction has landed, removing a punctuation mismatch and circular review prerequisite. A two-path profile correction is now landed and awaits its own independent review. No accepted PASS or host teardown is established.
stories.body: Main e1bff4eb includes the landed grammar parser correction (57f79604), a new profile-summary-coverage packet pair (ec5b1350), automatic handoff (03391a69), and a narrowly scoped two-path profile fix (e1bff4eb). Grammar implementation reports 8/8 selected changed-file validation checks passing, but that is not an independent verdict. The profile fix reports exactly 49 included paths, two more than its previous 47, with no broad root inclusion. Its implementation packet is marked complete, but its paired review remains outstanding. A reported preclaim check failed safely because the grammar summary was absent; no reviewer claim was created for that attempt. No canonical live dispatcher audit or host telemetry was inspected.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN fixed the review launcher's punctuation mismatch, but the next independent check uncovered a different missing piece: the lightweight reviewer checkout did not include the very implementation summary the reviewer needed. sections.heading: The parser correction is on main
sections.text: The shared publication-input parser now accepts a conventional final period after the last file path while keeping strict checks against unsafe and malformed paths. The implementation also removes a circular prerequisite that had made the adapter review depend on a later provisioning review. Its author reports passing focused tests and changed-file validation, not an independent PASS.

sections.heading: A smaller checkout still needs the right evidence
sections.text: The new sparse checkout profile was missing the grammar implementation's root-level summary. The canonical runner reportedly caught that omission before claiming a reviewer. Rather than widen the checkout indiscriminately, the follow-up adds exactly two named summaries, one for the grammar fix and one for the profile correction itself.

sections.heading: Acceptance remains a sequence, not a single green test
sections.text: The profile correction is now on main with its implementation packet marked complete. Its own fresh independent review must pass before the grammar review can resume. The adapter and original provisioning reviews follow in order; protected recovery still requires separate authorization.

insights.title: The safety gate is finding real evidence gaps
insights.explanation: The failed preclaim check shows why smaller worktrees need explicit dependency coverage. A reviewer cannot fairly approve a change if its checkout silently omits a required implementation summary.

insights.title: The fix is deliberately narrower than the problem
insights.explanation: The reported profile expands from 47 to 49 exact paths rather than adding a broad root directory. That preserves the storage benefit while exposing a maintenance cost: new review summaries must be explicitly included.

article.takeaway: Two implementation fixes have landed, but neither substitutes for independent acceptance. The next useful evidence is a fresh PASS for the bounded profile correction.

article.lead: A storage bottleneck that stranded Awakening development now has a code-level remedy. sections.heading: Why the old checkout stalled
sections.text: CUSTODIAN's art-heavy repository uses Git Large File Storage (LFS). Preparing a new worktree could require several gigabytes of assets before the agent could begin. The archived task records an Awakening checkout that failed when storage ran out after its claim was already acquired.

sections.heading: A smaller, verifiable path
sections.text: The new profile lists exact required files and hydrates them from existing local LFS objects, checking expected sizes and hashes. Capacity is checked before acquiring a claim and again before checkout writes. The original full checkout remains the default, while a guarded recovery path targets the exact interrupted claim rather than creating another one.

The review must challenge ownership, identity, storage, asset integrity and interrupted-checkout safeguards. Neither landing nor reported tests constitute accepted review or proof of clean host teardown.

insights.title: The smaller checkout remains reproducible

article.lead: A safety gap in CUSTODIAN's code-review pipeline now has a concrete repair plan. Two newly readied task packets propose checking the authenticity of synchronization history before changes can land, rather than discovering missing evidence only when independent review begins.

sections.heading: The problem sits between finishing and reviewing
sections.text: The current review verifier rejects a code history when it cannot authenticate a synchronization merge. The newly documented gap is earlier in the process: a workstream may publish its changes without proving that every earlier merge has the required lifecycle record.

sections.heading: The proposed fix has its own independent test
sections.text: The implementation packet calls for a fail-closed check before publication, with real-Git regression tests. A separate review packet must then examine both the new guard and the complete current validator. Neither packet being ready establishes that an agent is running.

insights.title: Preventing bad evidence is stronger than repairing it afterward
insights.explanation: The proposed change moves a provenance check earlier, where it can stop an unverifiable workstream before landing. That could reduce the accumulation of historical review-recovery cases.

insights.title: Recertification is not retroactive forgiveness
insights.explanation: Even a successful new review would not automatically accept or close older protected review runs. Their original evidence and separate authorization requirements remain intact.

article.takeaway: The guard is queued, not landed; its independent acceptance remains a future gate.
article.next_watch: An implementation commit and real-Git validation evidence, followed by a genuine independent review receipt.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN's Operator now has a committed architectural guard intended to prevent movement responsibilities and code size from drifting unnoticed. The safeguard does not add a new move or animation, but it helps protect the foundation on which those features depend. Its independent review has hit a narrow evidence problem.

sections.heading: A boundary around the movement chassis
sections.text: The guard inventories source ownership, checks growth limits and runs as part of the normal validation lifecycle. It keeps the existing Operator movement controller as the authority rather than silently shifting responsibilities elsewhere.

sections.heading: Promising tests, unfinished acceptance
sections.text: The implementation summary reports complete selected validation and two repeatable sidearm scenarios. It also preserves an earlier unexplained failure. The independent reviewer never launched because one regression-test file was omitted from the original packet's declared scope.

insights.title: Architectural progress can be invisible in gameplay
insights.explanation: The landing improves the project's ability to detect future movement-system regressions. It is infrastructure for safer gameplay work, not evidence that a new player-facing feature is live.

insights.title: Review evidence is now the gating issue
insights.explanation: The review stopped before reviewer judgment. The proposed remedy is a one-file, historically pinned attestation, which itself needs independent acceptance before the original review can resume.

article.takeaway: The Operator guard is implemented on main, but neither independently accepted nor proven deployed.
article.next_watch: A validated and independently accepted exact-source attestation, followed by separately authorized recovery of the preserved chassis review.

sections.heading: Why a single file can stop a review
sections.text: CUSTODIAN authenticates which files belong to a reviewed change before letting an independent reviewer proceed. The missing declaration caused the preserved review to stop before any verdict could be written.

sections.heading: A correction with its own safety gate
sections.text: The new packet requires immutable file identities and a separate independent PASS. Until that acceptance exists, the exception must do nothing. Even afterward, recovering the original review requires a new authorization.

insights.title: The fix must not rewrite history
insights.explanation: The proposal adds a post-hoc attestation instead of altering the original archived packet or pretending the reviewer ran. That preserves the audit trail while providing a narrowly checkable recovery path.

stories.body: The multi-sync verifier is on main and its implementation packet is archived. The published implementation summary reports 258 runner tests, four focused real-Git tests and 2/2 selected checks passed. The new resolver authenticates merge parentage, ordering, deterministic trees and unique lifecycle witnesses. In a read-only attempt against the protected correction history, it progressed beyond the former one-merge limitation but stopped at a missing checkpoint witness. No original run was modified. The paired independent review remains ready, not accepted. Host teardown, process and disk status are unverified.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN can now examine development histories that synchronize with the main codebase more than once. That removes a hard limitation in its independent review machinery, but the first preserved case has exposed a second, more fundamental gap: a missing historical checkpoint record.

sections.heading: A stronger account of what actually changed
sections.text: The new verifier checks each merge's parents, event order and resulting code, then separates files authored by the workstream from unrelated changes inherited from main. This matters when older review work overlaps newer Operator or infrastructure commits.

sections.heading: Why the original review is still held
sections.text: The implementation's own read-only check reached the next authenticity gate and could not find a unique checkpoint witness for the first historical merge. The system correctly refused to reconstruct evidence from Git history alone. Its own independent review is still pending.

insights.title: Removing one blocker can expose the next
insights.explanation: The earlier blanket rejection of multi-merge histories is gone, but a missing authenticated lifecycle event remains. The recovery chain now needs real provenance evidence, not merely more permissive code.

insights.title: Source isolation protects game-development work
insights.explanation: Separating inherited main changes from workstream-authored changes helps prevent newer art and gameplay edits from distorting the validation scope of older infrastructure reviews.

article.takeaway: Multiple-sync verification is landed, not independently accepted, and it has not recovered the protected review.
article.next_watch: An authenticated independent review receipt for this verifier, followed by an evidence-supported decision about the missing historical checkpoint.

article.lead: A correction intended to make CUSTODIAN's reviews more reliable has reached the main codebase, but its own closeout is stuck. An authorized manual landing succeeded; the normal finish did not. The latest documented validation attempt then timed out on one test, leaving independent review on hold.

sections.heading: Code integration is not administrative completion
sections.text: The audit records a carefully bounded fast-forward landing and an independent read-only assessment with no blocking findings. Neither replaces the canonical review receipt or the ordinary lifecycle finish. The review packet is explicitly blocked and manual.

sections.heading: A timeout with real consequences
sections.text: The final documented check selected nine tests. Eight passed, one timed out, and file coverage was complete. That is a failed validation, not a near-PASS that can be rounded up. The existing claim and worktree are deliberately preserved while a supported resolution is determined.

insights.title: The project's bottleneck is now lifecycle integrity
insights.explanation: The code can be integrated while the dispatcher still sees an unresolved execution lock and a failed finish. Fixing source validation alone does not make the workstream safe to retire.

insights.title: A clean diff is not a clean teardown
insights.explanation: The audit distinguishes source integration from release of the claim, lock and worktree. Those host-side gates need their own trustworthy evidence before downstream review can start.

article.takeaway: The merged-source correction is landed but not fully validated, independently accepted or cleanly retired.
article.next_watch: A supported, explicitly authorized resolution of the failed finish and timeout, followed by fresh validation and a canonical independent review.
